segments.text: A King Kong Company taxi driver that Minorikawa encounters on multiple occurrences.
A year prior, he was a school teacher who taught most of the members of S.O.S. He stepped away from teaching and became a taxi driver.

A girl who committed suicide due to unknown reasons. Her school denied any claims that she was bullied. Her suicide case was reopened 6 years later by both her former teacher and news reporter Minorikawa Minoru.
Ten years after her death, Minorikawa still remembers Chiharu's suicide and how the incident fueled him to become a freelancer reporter.

First-year student at Midoriyama Academy. A sweet young man who works as a part-time delivery driver for Dogen Hut and sends all his leftover money to his mother out in the country. Lately, however, he's gotten himself a girlfriend, and he's been sending money back home less frequently. His noodle house job doesn't pay enough to both support his mom and cover his dating expenses, so he's scheming for a way to make it rich quick.

He's taken the day off work today in order to attempt a dry run of the "Iron Stomach" eating competition, hoping to strike it rich while his girlfriend looks on. But after eating two parfaits, his stomach doesn't feel well, and has taken five trips to the toilet.
Edited from in-game TIPS
The producer for "The Wandering Angels."
She oversees Shinnosuke Oarai's interview with Minorikawa, ensuring to keep the director on schedule.
Early in the morning, Sukozawa sent her assistant Yukio Tozuka to retrieve the actor Akiomi Mondo from his apartment.
That evening, following their performance of Au Revoir, Sukozawa assigned Tozuka, Takuya Amo, and Shin'ichi Bando to return the defective dry ice machine.

(Portrayed by Kuwabara Yuuko, the scenario writer of a "Wandering Angels" storyline draft cut during development. The draft served as the basis of the 6-episode "The Tale of the Wandering Angels" TIPS storyline within the game, and was later reimplemented into the novel adaptation of 428.)
Employee at Co-Labo Café.

While appearing cute and demure at first glance, she's quite strong-willed, and frightening when angry. She works nights at a place called "The Scolding Pub," where customers rent private rooms in which they are scolded at length by attractive girls. One middle-aged businessman once told her: "Your face looks simply marvelous when you're angry."
Edited from in-game TIPS
A pair of girls from Midoriyama Academy's kindergarten.
They always hang out around the train station after school. They're quite fond of killing time inside of the Tokyu 5000 series display car, the new landmark by the Hachiko entrance.
The beat cop at the station's police box has nicknamed them "the Kinderpartners."
Edited from in-game TIPS
Employee of Far East Costume Rentals.

The only son of company president Shigemichi Fukuma, he is one of the few people who know what Shigemichi looks like, as his father is usually clad in a rabbit costume. Masamichi has harbored a strong dislike for both his father and mascot costumes ever since the old man showed up at school on Parents' Day one year dressed in his inevitable rabbit suit. Nonetheless, the son has acquiesced to his father's wishes, and some day he'll inherit the family business.
Edited from in-game TIPS

Rumi's father, formerly a detective in the First Investigation Division of the Metropolitan Police Department. He has retired to become a farmer in Nagano, and rejects the relationship between Rumi and Kano.

He posts regularly on the Aya Kamiki fan forum and "The 87th Precinct Telecommunity" under the username "Pretty Honey." He pretends to be a 19 year old female college student, and is an online friend of Kenji Osawa.

He has had several anonymous arguments with Rumi on the "87th" forum, with Shizuo criticizing the police for not doing their job, while Rumi insisting that police work is very difficult and deserves more credit.
He takes his username from a nickname for the apples he grows on his farm, which are pretty little things, and nearly as sweet as honey.
Edited from in-game TIPS
22 year old getting by on part-time employment.

Recently, after a number of employees quit in rapid succession, the owner took on several new hires; but for some reason, instead of everyone chipping in on the cleaning, Okado always winds up stuck doing it.
Edited from in-game TIPS
A custodian at downtown Shibuya's surveillance camera monitoring office.

His main job is overseeing the monitoring room for the local surveillance cameras, but on the side, he also works as a novelist and game scenario writer. He often sleeps on the job during his free time, but sometimes while he's asleep he gets his writing done. Just recently, a certain game was released, set in Shibuya — but since he wrote the scenario and emailed it to the game company while he was asleep, he didn't know about it until just the other day.
Edited from in-game TIPS
(The character is portrayed by the real Yukinori Kitajima, serving as a parody of himself)

Heart specialist and Suzune's attending physician. A preeminent surgeon who has successfully performed the "Batista procedure," wherein the left ventricle is reconstructed after a third of it has been removed.
Edited from in-game TIPS

A specialized victim support team belonging to the Special Criminal Investigation Unit that has been deployed at Osawa's house. The members of this team are all specialists who have received training in such skills as negotiation, high-speed motorcycle and automobile driving, running phone traces, special communications, and phone records acquisition.
Among them is Kiichi Sawatari, a detective at the Metropolitan Police Department's First Criminal Investigation Section.

Having heard of Kajiwara's past deeds from his friends at the Shibuya precinct, he recommended to his boss that Kajiwara be assigned to the investigation at the Osawa residence. After seeing the detective's interactions with Osawa, he is confident that his recommendation was in the right.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Sasayama's newlywed wife.
The two of them married just a month prior. The events of 428: Shibuya Scramble take place during Mii-chan's birthday, and Sasayama already has a present ready for her.
Kano's girlfriend and Shizuo's daughter.
Kano has been wanting to ask for Rumi's hand in marriage, but Shizuo has staunchly refused. She's waiting at the café Lautrec for Kano to come and meet her father.
A graduate from Midoriyama Academy, she originally won the Miss Midoriyama beauty contest when she was attending. She served as a judge for this year's contest.
Several people remark that her face has a striking resemblance to Masami Nagahama, a national TV star, but Kano insists that there is no connection between them.
Masa's girlfriend.
Masa takes the day off to invite her to watch him at the "Iron Stomach" eating competition, where he hopes to win enough money to be able to support his dates with her.
After Masa gets indigestion from eating too much food, his girlfriend calls Chiriko Osugi, an acquaintance of her, for advice on improving Masa's intestinal fortitude.
A rising J-pop and rock idol attempting to break into the global market.

Hitomi, Osawa, and Pretty Honey are fans of Kamiki, especially her newest single "Sekai wa Sore demo Kawari wa Shinai". She is advertised constantly throughout the streets of Shibuya, including a giant blimp floating in the air.

Her song "Sekai wa Sore demo Kawari wa Shinai" is used by the mastermind Alphard as part of her master plan. Alphard's bombs are set to explode if the song ever plays within close proximity. The song is the cause of the blue minivan explosion that kills Tanaka, and in multiple bad endings it is the cause of the explosion within the Scramble during the blockade.
(Her character is based on and portrayed by the real life Kamiki Aya, and her song "Sekai wa Sore demo Kawari wa Shinai" is the main theme of the game)
A mascot character that Achi wears on his shirt. The punks of Shibuya are able to recognize Achi simply by his Eco-kichi/Mean Clean shirt.
Eco-kichi/Mean Clean is the protagonist of the 3rd unlockable scenario in the post-game. He and his fellow anthropomorphic friends attempt to stop the pollution threatening Shibuya.
Hitomi's twin sister and Kenji Osawa's daughter.

She was kidnapped the night before, but mysteriously found herself free in the city with amnesia. She takes the part-time job for Yanagishita and dons the Tama costume, but removes it once the "Burning Hammer" sales demo is over. She wanders around Shibuya in search for a clue to her identity.

After her middle-eastern friend, Canaan, warned her about Alphard's plot to have Hitomi kidnapped, Maria planned out a twin swap in order to have the kidnapper, Daisuke, take her by mistake. Maria is allegedly infected with the Ua virus (proven incorrect in Bad Endings), which is used to spur the main cast into trying to save her.
Daisuke's wife, Achi and Suzune's mother, and the childhood friend of Kyozo Tateno.

17 years ago, soon after giving birth to Suzune, she was killed by a drug-addict, whom Tateno was unable to stop. Daisuke and Tateno note several times that Suzune is growing up to look just like Kotone, but lament Suzune's terminal heart condition will kill her young as well.
The props master for "The Wandering Angels."

He helped Yukio Tozuka in resolving the problem regarding the debt collectors harassing their actor Akiomi Mondo. After the show's production, Bando noticed that the dry ice machine purchased from Endo Electronics was malfunctioning and wouldn't stop producing dry ice. The show's producer, Sukozawa, sent Bando, Tozuka, and the novice actor Takuya Amo to return the ice machine.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Once Minorikawa informed them that they could discard the dry ice machine, the trio allowed Kano to take it, using it to deactivate Alphard's bomb and save the Scramble.
Production assistant for "The Wandering Angels." He approached Hitomi at the Hachiko statue at around 10 AM with fliers for their upcoming production of Au Revoir.

He was sent by the producer, Sukozawa, to retrieve the actor Akiomi Mondo from his apartment, who was being staked by debt collectors. During the performance, when novice actor Takuya Amo forgot to attach wires for a stunt, Tozuka improvised by entering onstage as "Assassin with an Edo Accent No. 1" and attaching the wire. Sukozawa assigned Tozuka, Amo, and Shin'ichi Bando to return the defective dry ice machine to Endo Electronics.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Once Minorikawa informed them that they could discard the dry ice machine, the trio allowed Kano to take it, using it to deactivate Alphard's bomb and save the Scramble.
A novice actor in "The Wandering Angels."

After Akiomi Mondo, the actor for the main rival in Au Revoir, was taken to the hospital for food poisoning, director Oarai assigned Amo to take up his role. Despite his credible performance, his inexperience showed when he forgot to attach the rigging to himself for a wire action scene, resulting in Tozuka Yukio having to stealthily attach it mid-performance. The show's producer, Sukozawa, sent Amo, Tozuka, and Shin'ichi Bandoto return the defective dry ice machine to Endo Electronics.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Once Minorikawa informed them that they could discard the dry ice machine, the trio allowed Kano to take it, using it to deactivate Alphard's bomb and save the Scramble.
Stage director for "The Wandering Angel."
He handles things behind the scenes for the production of Au Revoir. He's very irritated that Shin'ichi Bando, in charge of the props, seems to have gone AWOL.
Edited from in-game TIPS
He and Takaya accidentally lock Achi and Hitomi inside the troupe's storage building while hiding from The Man with the Cane.
The star actor for "The Wandering Angels."
He plays the lead role of "Ryu" in the troupe's 22nd piece, Au Revoir. The previous night, he slept completely naked and caught a cold, leading to a sore throat.

In addition to appearing on stage, he's been taking on TV drama and film work as well. The next role he's slated for is in Sun TV's upcoming suspense-drama Sumo Queen 2, where he will play the referee who utters the lame line "Looks like things are getting heavy" upon discovering a victim's dying message inscribed in one corner of the sumo ring.
Edited from in-game TIPS
He and Toga accidentally lock Achi and Hitomi inside the troupe's storage building while hiding from The Man with the Cane.
A mercenary and mentor to Sadaqah and Canaan, the latter whom considered him as her friend.

Born west of the Jordan River 4 years after the Tripartite Aggression, Siam became a member of the Palestine liberation movement as a member of Colonel Gaddafi's camp. Once he became a mercenary, he participated in the Iraq War and found a young girl who lost her family, taking her in and naming her Canaan, training her to become a mercenary like him.

Two years later (4 years prior to the events of 428: Shibuya Scramble), Siam and Canaan took a mission to retrieve prototype samples of the Ua virus, but was ultimately killed by Sadaqah, now named Alphard.
A giant mass of pollution who attempted to kill Achi and Mean Clean in order to enact its master plan of covering Shibuya in trash.
One of Mean Clean's friends, who helps him in fighting against Metabon. He's a sentient can of coffee beans.
One of Mean Clean's friends, who helps him in fighting against Metabon. He's a paper juice box with extensive knowledge in chemistry.
An old friend of Mean Clean. He's a small bonsai tree inside a pot.
One of Mean Clean's friends. He once fought against the vegetable cult alongside Mean Clean, and he returns for the fight against Metabon.
A meth addict who assaulted someone and ran away from the police 17 years prior.
He held Kotone hostage and killed her in a fit of paranoia caused by meth withdrawal. Tateno blames himself for being unable to apprehend him in time to save Kotone.

Kenji Osawa's estranged second wife and the twins' stepmother. She's the daughter of Suruga Makino, the corporate director at Okoshi Pharmaceutical and Osawa's boss. Her greedy and selfish disposition has her care more about her financial status and her father's company than the safety of her own stepdaughters during the kidnapping case.

She is Mamoru Tanaka's former lover, but she was forced into marrying Osawa to secure his position in the company. Due to her lingering feelings for Tanaka and Osawa's decision to move to the U.S., she blackmails Osawa under the pseudonym "A" with images of her father's secret human antiviral trials to force him to stay with the company.
The Governor of Tokyo, who announces a blockade around Shibuya following a bioterrorism threat.
The Governor is portrayed by Hirokazu Hanamura via a special appearance.
A member of S.O.S. He's always with a counterpart wearing blue clothes and follows Susumu diligently.
A member of S.O.S. He's always seen with a counterpart wearing red clothes and follows Susumu diligently.
A young man who recently joined S.O.S. He receives a shakedown from other members of the group.

Members of KOK (known as S.O.S. in the English release), founded by Achi Endo and currently led by Suzumu Nishizawa. Initially, S.O.S. was nothing more than a small group of like-minded young people who hung out together, but as its membership grew, the general public began referring to the group as a "gang." Word has it that back when Achi was in charge, gang members never started any conflicts themselves, but simply responded in kind when others brought fights their way.
Edited from in-game TIPS

cast.characterName: フランク・スタンリー
cast.originalCharacterName: フランク・スタンリー

segments.text: Jack Stanley's younger brother, and a member of the Chicago Police Department's Bomb and Arson Squad.
Two years prior, he was killed attempting to disarm an explosion at a high-class hotel in Chicago, orchestrated by Alphard.
Stanley's boss at the CIA, and the person in charge of the kidnapping investigation, giving instructions to the investigators operating on the case.
In truth, he's been working with Alphard from behind the scenes as her CIA contact.
Masa's grandmother.

In Yutaro Segawa's younger years, he attempts to scam her as part of a scheme to get money and pay off his debts to Takarada Financing. She mistakes Segawa for her grandson, Masa, and his inability to scam her leads to Segawa being roped into the Tenryu-gumi and work under Asao Ozu to pay off his debts.

The leader of seven food sprites from Italy, who traveled to Japan based on rumors of a 5-star restaurant and eventually settled at Dogen Hut, helping the widowed Maki Yoneda cook. He specializes in meat dishes.
One of the seven food sprites from Italy who settled at Dogen Hut. He can track down fresh ingredients in the blink of an eye.
One of the seven food sprites from Italy who settled at Dogen Hut. He's a wizard when it comes to sauce.
One of the seven food sprites from Italy who settled at Dogen Hut. He's a wine connoisseur and the most sarcastic fellow in the world.
One of the seven food sprites from Italy who settled at Dogen Hut. He's a neat-freak that loves a clean and tidy kitchen.
One of the seven food sprites from Italy who settled at Dogen Hut. None could outmatch his pasta-making skills, as he has a divine touch.
One of the seven food sprites from Italy who settled at Dogen Hut. The quiet one, he can tell you all about pizza dough.

cast.characterName: マルセル・ポワティエ
cast.originalCharacterName: マルセル・ポワティエ

segments.text: A general goods trader in Paris, who sells Yanagishita the Burning Hammer bottles. He tries to give away a set of Indonesian dolls set to curse anyone who owns them, unintentionally handing them off to Yanagishita.
Marcel's dealer, and an acquaintance of Yanagishita who rejected his advances. She scams Yanagishita into buying Marcel's cursed dolls.
The previous champion at the fighting pub Bride.
She starts each match by crying and radiating weakness, only to win each match at the end. This earned her the stage name of "Crybaby Mizuho", although Miku could easily see through her ruse.
Director Kuze's son, who is still in school and plays baseball. Like everyone who works at the Shibuya Precinct, Tatsuya is aware of his father's childish register.
A person who works for Chun Food Service Center and answers the company telephone. For about a year, they've been receiving calls from Katayama regarding their "misleading" branding.

A man who loves Shibuya more than any other place, Achi is the former head of KOK (S.O.S. in the English release), the most influential street clan in Shibuya. He has since left KOK and now spends his days cleaning up the streets and picking up trash. During his daily street cleaning routine, he encounters and saves a girl who was nearly shot by a man with a gun.
From Wikipedia

A young detective from the Shibuya Police Department, Kanou is one of the detectives standing near Hitomi, a girl whose twin sister Maria was kidnapped for ransom. The kidnapper had specified Hitomi to bring the money to its pickup location, Shibuya station plaza. As the criminal shows up and runs with the money, Kanou begins to chase him.
From Wikipedia

A virus expert and the father of Hitomi and Maria Osawa. As the lab director of Okoshi Pharmaceutical, Osawa leads a hermit-like life. A week after his US business trip, he receives a series of mysterious e-mails that indicate someone had conducted an unauthorized clinical trial of an antiviral drug he had been researching.
From Wikipedia
In 3 Nen B Gumi Kinpachi-sensei:
Rinko's ex-boyfriend.
A freelance reporter looking into Fuyutsuki Chiharu's suicide.
In 428: Shibuya Scramble:

A hot headed freelance writer, Minorikawa receives a desperate phone call from his former superior, Toyama. Toyama, now the president of a small publishing company, was swamped in debt and now forced to complete the latest issue of his magazine in a single day. Minorikawa offers to help finish the magazine.
From Wikipedia
A cat suit that appears in both 428: Shibuya Scramble and Time Travelers. In both games, the suit is inhabited by an unidentified female character.
In 428: Shibuya Scramble:

Tama, a person of unknown identity, is working inside a cat suit as a by-the-day temp worker for Yanagishita in order to buy a special necklace she found at a general store. She begins her work of promoting a diet drink, "Burning Hammer."
Edited from Wikipedia
Her true identity is revealed to be Maria Osawa, Hitomi's twin sister and Kenji Osawa's daughter.
The Tama mascot also appear as:
—One of Sasayama's disguises in a Bad Ending, where it's revealed that the costume is a CATS (Costume As Transmission System), a robotic suit capable of dimensional travel.
—Several guides within the Labyrinth that lead Minorikawa through it.
In Time Travelers:
A mysterious woman who appears in the story wearing a cat costume. Her identity is a mystery.
Tama's real identity is an iteration of Mikoto Shindou, from one of her many time loops in the story.

A resident of Shibuya whose twin sister, Maria, has been kidnapped. With the help of the police, she attempts to pay off ¥50 million to the kidnapper, but things take an unexpected turn at the exchange.

cast.characterName: アルファルド・アル・シュヤ
cast.originalCharacterName: アルファルド・アル・シュヤ

segments.text: A Middle-Eastern girl who has ties to the American CIA and the mastermind of the kidnapping plot. She first appears as "Canaan", masquerading as Oosawa Maria's friend to gain the trust of Oosawa Hitomi.
Leader of a foreign crime syndicate operating within Shibuya. Working for the kidnapper/mastermind of the Osawa twins' case, he leads the ransom money relay among the members of his syndicate.
Organizer of the Burning Hammer sales demo. He hired Tama and Chiriko to help promote and sell the Burning Hammer bottle.

Yanagishita spent one million yen to purchase 300 bottles, and plans to sell each bottle for 15,000 yen to gain a profit. He's in debt with the Takarada Financing, and is trying to avoid the debt collectors until the sales demo is finished.

cast.characterName: ジャック・スタンリー
cast.originalCharacterName: ジャック・スタンリー

segments.text: A security assistance officer from the U.S. Embassy. He joins Kano during his investigation of the kidnapping case.
In actuality, Stanley is a CIA agent attempting to uncover and take down Alphard as revenge for his brother's death.

Assistant lab director at Okoshi Pharmaceutical, working directly under Kenji Osawa. His faithful commitment to his work has managed to earn Osawa's trust, acting as his confidant during the kidnapping case and in regards to the blackmail e-mails. He shares an undisclosed relationship with Hitomi Osawa and acts as her primary relay contact during the case.

In truth, Tanaka is a traitor to Okoshi Pharmaceutical and works directly under Alphard to steal the Ua antiviral. The former lover of Osawa's current wife, Ai, he resents Osawa and has worked with Alphard to undermine him.
A novice freelance reporter who is scared of talking to people. Minorikawa hires her to help write articles for the next issue of Four Star General Gossip.

Chiaki's tendecy to become flustered is famous among her freelance writer colleagues. Once, she conducted an hour-long interview during which she only managed to ask her interview subject's name — yet another chapter in "The Legend of Hopelessly Flustered Chiaki."
Edited from in-game TIPS
Achi and Suzune's father. Owner of Endo Electronics.

Daisuke is an alum from Tokyo Denko University, attending on a full scholarship. His knowledge in electronics and worry about delinquent activity led him to develop the local surveillance system used throughout Shibuya's shopping districts.

Daisuke is the culprit of the kidnapping case, having mistakenly kidnapped Maria while attempting to capture and kill Hitomi for a heart transplant for his daughter, Suzune. He was coerced into the crime as part of Alphard's master plot to steal the Ua antiviral.
An assassin attempting to hunt down Hitomi Osawa soon after she hands off the ransom money.
His identity is Kyozo Tateno, a detective at the Shibuya Central Police Station. Kano looks up to Tateno and has based his detective "Dick Diary" based on the various dictums Tateno provides.

Tateno is a childhood friend of Achi's parents, having been in love with Kotone even long after her death. Daisuke asked Tateno to kill Hitomi so that her heart could be transplanted into their daughter, Suzune, and save her from her terminal heart condition.

cast.characterName: リーランド・パーマー
cast.originalCharacterName: リーランド・パーマー

segments.text: Hitomi and Maria's English professor. He's been a lecturer at Midoriyama Academy for the past 6 months. He and Hitomi both witnessed Maria's kidnapping.

Leland has actually been a member of Snake the entire time. He infected Hitomi with the Ua virus, and contacted Daisuke Endo as an "organ trafficker" to lead him into attempting to kidnap Hitomi. He poses as his leader, Alphard, during the finale while the real Alphard attempts to infiltrate Okoshi Pharmaceutical.

A detective with the Shibuya Precinct's Criminal Investigation Division. He is sociable but awkward, and despite his reserved personality he can be quite unsettling. His colleagues at the precinct refer to him by nicknames such as "Japanese Columbo" and "Little Ken Takakura," given his own quirky demeanor as a detective.
He is stationed at the Osawa residence during the investigation into the kidnapping case. He keeps a watchful yet teasing eye on Osawa himself during the case's development.
Edited from in-game TIPS
He once had a run-in with Naito Jun (from Machi, portrayed by the same actor), and they were both shocked to discover they look exactly the same.

A young woman hired by Yanagishita to work at the Burning Hammer sales demo alongside Tama. She has a bottomless stomach that can consume any food, and lately she's been attempting a "protein diet" where she takes protein drinks alongside her meals.
A fighter at the cosplay fighting pub Bride. Yanagishita is one of her biggest fans at the bar.
In middle school, she had been Japan's bonsai champion. She took up martial arts at Midorikawa's suggestion.

Employee of Cho-Nippon Printing Company's Sales Department, Division #1. He was recently assigned to handling Heaven Publishing after his predecessor, Sachio Usui, was admitted to the hospital following a car crash earlier that day. He follows a strict deadline and pressures Minorikawa to submit the next edition of Four-Star General Gossip to press earlier than planned.
Operations Director for the kidnapping case.
Whenever he gets overly flustered, excited, or panicked, he slips into a childish register, prone to babbling and pitching his voice.

Kuze has a brother (Monday), six years his senior, who despite being nominally mature refuses to get a real job and shows no inclination to settle down with a family. Kuze has been worrying about his shiftless brother for years now; the guy's become a chronic source of consternation.
Edited from in-game TIPS
(Kuze and Monday are portrayed by the same actor)

The corporate director of Okoshi Pharmaceutical. He is Ai's father, making him both Kenji Osawa's boss and father-in-law. His ruthless and greedy behavior has him control Osawa's actions as he aims to quickly profit from their antiviral research.

He engaged in illegal human testing with the antiviral in South Africa to advance the drug's development as quickly as possible. Despite his cold demeanor, he is a frequent customer at a local cat cafe.
Endou Achi's sister, who is hospitalized at Shibuya Central Hospital.

She suffers from a dilated cardiomyopathy heart disease and requires a heart transplant to survive. Her extremely rare Bombay Blood type makes finding a donor nearly impossible, and she is not expected to live long.
A patient suffering from Wilson's disease. He resides in the same hospital as Suzune.
His birthday is on 4/28, the day of the game's events. He dies two days later at 15 years old, and his heart is transplanted into Suzune.

A member of the Tenryu-gumi yakuza syndicate. The Tenryu-gumi operates a lending firm called Takarada Financing, and he's been tasked with collecting outstanding debts alongside his underling Yutaro Segawa. They've already collected from one client today.
Ozu is quite frightening when angry —his nickname is "Ozu the Ogre"— but despite his strong emotions he is very logic-driven.
Edited from in-game TIPS

A member of the Tenryu-gumi yakuza syndicate. The Tenryu-gumi operates a lending firm called Takarada Financing, and he's been tasked with collecting outstanding debts alongside Asao Ozu. They've already collected from one client today.

Segawa is the archetypical punk who likes to get into scuffles, but he's also a really good cook. He's unbeatable in street fights, earning him the nickname "the Crazy Tiger of Shibuya." Back in his boxing days, however, Segawa was so tough people called him "the Dogfighter of Shibuya." One day, as he was walking along, he happened to step onto a strange panel that made him fall into a state of confusion and go on a rampage. He was quickly arrested, and his boxing license was revoked.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Toyama's daughter, currently ten years old.

The night Hana was born at Shibuya Central Hospital, there was an unexpected fireworks display outside the window of the maternity ward. As he looked out at the bursting rockets, Teruo decided to name his daughter Hana, after the Japanese word for fireworks, "hanabi."
She also writes intricate poetry that she sells to help pay off her dad's debt. Hana's talents will soon be discovered by Aya Kamiki, and she will go on to become a popular songwriter.
Edited from in-game TIPS

Hana's father. He founded Heaven Publishing 5 years prior to the events of 428: Shibuya Scramble, with its flagship product being the magazine Four-Star General Gossip. He has taken out numerous debts with a Yakuza loan shark business to keep his business operating.

At the time of Chiharu Fuyursuki's death, Toyama was the copy editor for the local newspaper, the Centra Times. Known as "The Red Pen Gatekeeper," he would go around checking young reporters' copies like mad. Due to his vigorous efforts, a great many articles never made it to the page. Toyama and Minorikawa would often clash regarding the quality of the latter's writing.
His book The Invincible Journalist, published under Heaven Publishing, was a candidate for the Japan Nonfiction Prize.
Edited from in-game TIPS

The second-in-command at S.O.S. He used to roll with a gang from Ikebukuro until a few months ago. Known as "The Killer Whale of 'Bukuro," he answered any and all resistance with his fists. His crazy antics led to him being kicked out of the gang, however, and lately he's been hanging around Shibuya.
Edited from in-game TIPS

The current leader of S.O.S. He was previously friends with Achi, but once Achi stepped down as leader of S.O.S. and gave the role to Susumu, he started resenting his former friend for leaving him behind. The group has been struggling under his leadership, with half its members following the newcomer Kiryu instead of him.
Senior officer of the Shibuya Precinct's Criminal Affairs Division, five years older than Kano.
Known as the "Cosplay Detective" due to the strange outfits he wears while on stakeouts. He's partnered with Shinya Kano for the kidnapping investigation.
It's quite rare for Sasayama to actually wear a suit. On the rare occasions when he does, and he's walking the halls of his home precinct, he frequently goes unrecognized.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Second-year student at Midoriyama Academy's law school. She works part-time at the café Lautrec.

Some hustlers managed to corner her while she was on her way to her part-time, resulting in her showing up five minutes late for her shift. The manager told her that those five minutes were coming out of her pay, so she's a bit irritated.
Edited from in-game TIPS
The owner and cook of Dogen Hut.

When she was nineteen, she happened to stop by the soba shop and was captivated by the chilled curry soba. By day's end, she had decided to make the restaurant her new home. Married the owner at age twenty-two and they managed the establishment together. Last year, her husband of thirty years passed away. Now she safeguards the generations-old secret of chilled curry soba on her own.
She currently employs two part-timers, Masa from Midoriyama Academy, and Mohinder, an Indian exchange student.
Edited from in-game TIPS

Former broadcast writer. Has appeared on various popular variety shows on commercial network Sun TV. He currently heads up a small theater troupe known as "The Wandering Angels," operating out of Shibuya.
The troupe is putting on a performance at Theatre Ace in Sakuragaokacho later that day.
Edited from in-game TIPS
A part-time staffer at Imabiki Chinese Restaurant.

Her boss chewed her out pretty bad for showing up at work with her nails manicured black. She was ordered to go to the restroom and scrub them clean, but no amount of nail polish remover was able to do the trick, and so she's been dealing with her boss's wrath all day long.
Edited from in-game TIPS
Proprietor of a new knickknack shop in Udagawacho.
While he was wandering along the JR tracks picking up lost and abandoned items, Achi foisted off his trash onto him, and so he's in a bit of a foul mood.

Yasuda watches roughly 350 martial arts fights a year. He is particularly fond of Brazilian jiu-jitsu, and is thinking about studying himself. There's a dojo he's been eyeing, but he's rather timid, and has thus far only waffled noncommittally outside the entrance to the place.
Achi knows Shibuya like his own backyard, but Yasuda is new enough that Achi doesn't recognize him.
Edited from in-game TIPS
